_comment: Lane RELEASE-1: the known issues a tester meets, for README_TESTERS.txt (tools/release/readme_testers.py). Each item names the docs/STOPS.md rows it comes from; the generator copies their Area and fails when a row is gone (the issue was resolved or renumbered: update this list). Keep the text in a player's words. Each item has an "area" (autorelease.AREAS): the patch notes group the known issues by it, README_TESTERS prints it as a prefix for Campaign, Create-a-Hero and Launcher and install.

issues.text: The game checks installs in English and ten other languages. A game in any other language starts with a warning, because its language files cannot be checked. OpenBFME's own texts, such as the online screens, are in English only.
Heroes carry over from one campaign mission to the next with their experience, but the campaign's saves are OpenBFME's own: a campaign saved in the original game cannot be continued here.

War of the Ring can be played alone or over LAN, and saved and resumed, but not online yet. A battle with more armies than its map has start positions is decided automatically instead of being fought.
Heroes can be built, coloured and saved, but how the house colour blends into the model is an educated guess, and the colour is not reapplied to lower-detail textures the way the original may do.
Team colours use the original's blend, but the colour a player gets on a map that sets none is an educated guess.

The computer opponent builds a base, trains armies and heroes, uses its spell book and powers, attacks and finishes games, but does not yet defend its base the way the original does, it expands to a second base with only some factions, and it skips some powers.
Enemy buildings destroyed out of your sight disappear at once instead of staying in the fog until you look again.
Some sounds are missing: units being damaged, scripted music and parts of the big-battle ambience.
Movies have no subtitles.
Menus are laid out for 1024x768 and scaled: at other window sizes text and click targets can be slightly off.
Radar: attacks, mission scripts and finished buildings raise pings, but the Ring and beacon markers and the stealth alerts are missing.
Every game is recorded as a replay and can be watched from Load Replay with pause, speed and seeking, but a replay cannot be saved under a name, and the score screen's graphs are simplified.
Hero bar: a Create-a-Hero hero shows its class's icon, not its own picture.

Help boxes and tool tips: a hero's help does not count battles fought, and the main menu's My Heroes and Quit buttons show no tool tip. The lobby, staging and map list tool tips (players, map results, passwords), the Create-a-Hero builder's power tips, the in-game disband and rename tips, the control bar's resource, command point and menu button tips and the War of the Ring map's tool tips are not shown yet.
Build bubbles around a building do not flash yet.
Selection rings always use the highest-detail look, whatever the detail setting.
Units, buildings and trees cast shadows, but they are not yet drawn exactly like the original's, and a building's placement preview casts none.
Graphics detail: the detail level sets the particle limit, texture quality, shadows and health bars, but the model, animation, terrain, water and shader detail settings are greyed out.
Turning a hero's autocast on or off does not play the hero's voice line.

Online: everyone in a game must use this version or later. If the game's first player runs an older version, a crashed player can still freeze the game instead of being dropped when the disconnect screen's bar runs out.
Online and LAN: a player still loading the map about a minute after the others have finished is treated as gone and dropped when the disconnect screen's bar runs out.
